gaps.summary: No published contract names account, recovery or session lifecycle events, so the J01 identity step carries no event reference yet.
Journey signals have no published analytics event schema; the content-free field set in these blueprints is a proposal for the ingestion owner.

Registry diagrams D01, D03, D04, D05 and D21 name product/08 or Figma pages as their artifact, but their renderings are the Git text in product/journey-blueprints.md while Figma is held; docs#75 owns repointing artifact_path.
Recovery start, cancellation and completion have no published event, so the J02 recovery steps carry no event reference yet.
The registry has no notification or email channel flow or screen, so notification steps in J02, J06, J09, J10 and J12 map to no flow.

Stories US-WEB-02 and US-WEB-05 on flows F-WEB-02 and F-WEB-05 name persona P05, but journey J03 lists only P03 and P04; the blueprint copies the journey list until docs#75 adds P05 to J03 or moves the stories, and docs#66 validates the persona.
Reporting-currency conversion needs currencies beyond the single-currency MVP ledger of ADR-017; admission and rate source are pending.
Settlement and dispute windows for split groups have no published value, so the J06 clock controls state them as pending.
ADR-021 makes safe exit quiet by design with no notification content beyond a pointer; whether the other member sees any pointer after a safe exit, and its wording, is an open design decision.
The online revocation bound and the offline lease bound after which cached shared household data is hidden are both published by T-CON-04 and have no value yet.
Safe-exit and coercive-control assumptions are unvalidated; research must not recruit both household members into one session.
J09 lists no operator refund flow; refund operations F-ADM-06 belong to J10 only, so billing reversal relies on the J10 operator step.
Response clock values for export, deletion and grievance requests are not published in an accepted source; T-CMP-01 starts each clock at acknowledgement, and controls state the values as pending.

Story US-ADM-06 on refund flow F-ADM-06 names persona P12, but journey J10 lists only P03, P07 and P10, so the refund step names the support operator; docs#75 owns adding P12 to J10 and docs#66 validates the persona.

Every step carries a data class on a four-level scale (public, internal, confidential, restricted) proposed here; ADR-020 section 15 assigns personal-data classification to the T-CMP-04 jurisdiction profile, which confirms or replaces the scale.
ADR-020 section 16 sets elevation, unmask and break-glass limits but no expiry for an unapproved access request; J11 states it as pending.
The docs#67 scope names operator blueprints for refunds, provider change and incidents, but the registry assigns those flows to J10 and J12, not J11.
Regulator and customer notice deadlines for incidents are not published in an accepted source; the incident clock step cannot state them.
Obligation O-21 requires advance notice and grandfathering on a price or entitlement change, but no accepted source publishes the notice period, so the J12 migration clock states it as pending.
